Ancient Synagogue in Ostia

Synagogue site · Lazio, Italy

The Ostia Synagogue is one of the oldest known synagogues in the world and the oldest discovered in Europe. Located in the ancient Roman port city of Ostia, near Rome, it dates to the 1st century CE and remained in use until approximately the 5th century.

The synagogue complex included a large prayer hall with benches along three walls, a monumental entrance, a communal dining room, and facilities for ritual washing. Its main entrance was oriented southeast, toward Jerusalem. In the 4th century, a stone structure serving as a Torah Ark was added, replacing earlier wooden installations donated by members of the community.

Decorative remains include carved menorah symbols, inscriptions, and architectural elements that provide important evidence of a well-established Jewish community living within the Roman Empire. Scholars continue to debate whether the building was originally constructed as a synagogue or was first used as a private residence before being converted.

Today, the ruins form part of the archaeological site of ancient Ostia and offer a rare glimpse into Jewish religious and communal life during the Roman period.
